To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
L-FABP and i-FABP expression is inversely regulated in the model of NEC.
L-FABP and iFABP are expressed in the intestine of newborn rats, and that their expression changes inversely in response to the model of NEC, and in the presence of the antibiotic gentamycin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of FABP expression in NEC.
the development of a new method of treatment of necrotizing colitis, which is a serious and life-threatening complication of neonatal sepsis.
a better understanding of the role played by L-FABP and the role of I-FABP and their relationship with necrotizing entercolitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of L-FABP and/or I-FABP as biomarkers in the diagnosis of NEC in the neonatal intensive care unit is not recommended.
the results of this study indicate that the expression of L-FABP and the expression of I-FABP in newborn rats are differentially changed in the model of NEC.
the use of L-fabp as a marker of intestinal injury in the neonatal period has not yet been proven.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two FABP isoforms, I-FABP and L-FABP, are inversely controlled in the model of NEC.
the expression of L-FABP and/or I-FABP is altered in the model of NEC.
the two FABPs have different expression patterns in the model of NEC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of L-FABP and the expression of I-FABP are inversely correlated in the rat model of NEC.
the L-FABP and the I-FABP levels are altered in the model of NEC.
the gut barrier is compromised in necrotizing entercolitis, and the gut barrier is a key component of the gut-brain axis.
